docs.title: Formula 1: Scatterplot Matrix (SPLOM) Subplot Combinations
docs.text:
\[ N_{\text{unique}} = \frac{k(k-1)}{2} \] Symbol Meaning Units / Range \(k\) Total number of quantitative dimensions Integer (\(k \ge 2\)) \(N_{\text{unique}}\) Unique off-diagonal bivariate scatter plots Integer (\(N_{\text{unique}} \ge 1\))
  • Conditions: Assumes all \(k\) attributes are paired without self-plots; symmetric duplicate plots are omitted.

docs.title: Formula 2: Stevens' Psychophysical Power Law
docs.text:
\[ R = k \cdot S^\beta \] Symbol Meaning Units / Range \(R\) Subjective perceived sensation Dimensionless scale \(S\) Physical intensity of visual stimulus \(\text{px}, \text{mm}^2\) \(k\) Scaling proportionality constant Real scalar (\(k > 0\)) \(\beta\) Psychophysical response exponent Length: \(\beta \approx 1.0\), Area: \(\beta \approx 0.8\), Volume: \(\beta \approx 0.5\)
  • Conditions: Empirical psychological testing under steady-state sensory conditions.

docs.title: Formula 3: Tufte's Lie Factor
docs.text:
\[ \text{Lie Factor} = \frac{\left| \frac{\text{Graphic}_{\text{end}} - \text{Graphic}_{\text{start}}}{\text{Graphic}_{\text{start}}} \right|}{\left| \frac{\text{Data}_{\text{end}} - \text{Data}_{\text{start}}}{\text{Data}_{\text{start}}} \right|} \] Symbol Meaning Acceptable Range \(\text{Lie Factor}\) Graphical distortion ratio \(0.95 \le \text{LF} \le 1.05\)
  • Conditions: Visual metrics measured with physical calipers or pixel counts.

docs.title: Formula 4: Tufte's Data-Ink Ratio
docs.text: \[ \text{Data-Ink Ratio} = \frac{\text{Data-Ink}}{\text{Total Ink Used to Print the Graphic}} = 1.0 - \text{Proportion of Chartjunk} \] Symbol Meaning Target Value \(\text{Data-Ink Ratio}\) Efficiency of non-redundant data communication \(\to 1.0\)

docs.title: Formula 5: Absenteeism Rate
docs.text: \[ \text{Absenteeism Rate} = \left( \frac{\text{Total Unplanned Absence Days}}{\text{Total Available Work Days} \times \text{Average Headcount}} \right) \times 100\% \] Symbol Meaning Target Value \(\text{Absenteeism Rate}\) Proportion of lost work days Percentage (\(< 3.0\%\))

docs.title: Formula 6: Human Capital Return on Investment (HCROI)
docs.text: \[ \text{HCROI} = \frac{\text{Revenue} - (\text{Total Operating Expenses} - \text{Total Labor Costs})}{\text{Total Labor Costs}} \] Symbol Meaning Target Value \(\text{HCROI}\) Profit generated per dollar of employee expenditure Ratio (\(> 1.25\))

docs.title: Formula 7: Cost-Per-Hire (CPH)
docs.text: \[ \text{CPH} = \frac{\sum \text{Internal Recruiting Costs} + \sum \text{External Recruiting Costs}}{\text{Total New Hires in Period}} \] Symbol Meaning Target Value \(\text{CPH}\) Average financial expenditure to acquire one new employee Currency ($/hire)

docs.title: Formula 8: Point-Line Intersect in Parallel Coordinates
docs.text: \[ u_{\text{intersect}} = \frac{d}{1 - m}, \quad v_{\text{intersect}} = \frac{c}{1 - m} \] Symbol Meaning Units / Range \(m\) Slope of straight line in Cartesian space (\(y = mx + c\)) Real scalar (\(m \neq 1\)) \(c\) Intercept of straight line in Cartesian space Real scalar \(d\) Uniform horizontal distance separating parallel coordinate axes Real distance units \((u_{\text{intersect}}, v_{\text{intersect}})\) Coordinate location of intersecting pencil point in parallel coordinates Display coordinate plane

docs.title: 11.3 Quick-Revision Definition Sheet
docs.text:
• Data-Ink Ratio: The proportion of ink in a graphical presentation devoted exclusively to displaying non-redundant quantitative data.
  • Chartjunk: Superfluous visual ornamentation (3D perspective, fake lighting, heavy moiré gridlines) that distracts from data decoding.
  • Parallel Coordinates: Multi-dimensional visualization technique mapping \(k\) dimensions to \(k\) equidistant parallel axes; records become continuous polygonal lines.
  • Point-Line Duality: Projective property in parallel coordinates where a point in Cartesian space maps to a line, and a line maps to an intersection point.
  • Occlusion (Hairballing): Visual failure mode where dense overlapping lines in parallel coordinates obscure data structures.
  • Chernoff Faces: Icon-based method encoding multi-attribute records as geometric features of cartoon human faces.
  • Stick Figures: Icon-based method encoding variables to the angles and lengths of a 5-piece limb figure, generating macroscopic visual textures.
  • Dimensional Stacking: Hierarchical technique embedding 2D coordinate spaces inside coarse 2D grid cells; practical limit \(\le 9\) dimensions.
  • Worlds-within-Worlds: Hierarchical method nesting 3D coordinate frames inside outer 3D parameter worlds.
  • Tree-Map: Recursive space-filling algorithm partitioning a rectangle into sub-rectangles whose areas reflect hierarchical node size.
  • 3D Cone Tree: 3D interactive hierarchical tree arranging child nodes around the circular bases of cones; scales to 1,000 nodes.
  • InfoCube: 3D hierarchical visualization using nested semi-transparent cubes.
  • Circle Segments: Pixel-oriented method dividing a circle into \(m\) radial wedges, laying out pixels in concentric spirals from center to perimeter.
  • Space-Filling Curve: Continuous curve passing through every point in a bounded multi-dimensional space, preserving topological locality.
  • Peano-Hilbert Curve: Fractal space-filling curve with superior multi-directional locality preservation.
  • Full-Time Equivalent (FTE): Standardized metric equal to the work volume of one full-time employee.
  • Level of Detail (LOD): Tableau aggregation syntax ({FIXED}, {INCLUDE}, {EXCLUDE}) specifying calculation granularity independently of active sheet shelves.
  • Kernel Density Estimation (KDE): Non-parametric statistical technique smoothing discrete histograms into continuous probability density functions.
  • Declarative Grammar: Visualization paradigm (Altair, Vega-Lite) specifying what to visualize rather than how to draw it procedurally.

docs.title: Q1. Define the term 'Locality Preservation' in the context of space-filling curves.
docs.text: Answer: Locality preservation is the mathematical property of a spatial mapping function \(\pi: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^2\) ensuring that data records that are close to each other in one-dimensional sequence order (\(|i - j| \le \delta\)) remain spatially adjacent in two-dimensional visual display space (\(\|\pi(i) - \pi(j)\|_2 \le C\sqrt{\delta}\)), preventing artificial visual discontinuities.

docs.title: Q2. State the difference between a Blue Pill and a Green Pill in Tableau.
docs.text: Answer: A Blue Pill represents Discrete data, generating distinct categorical row/column headers and slicing aggregations. A Green Pill represents Continuous data, generating an unbroken numerical or temporal coordinate axis with continuous gradients.

docs.title: Q3. What is 'point-line duality' in Parallel Coordinates?
docs.text: Answer: Point-line duality is the projective geometric property whereby an \(m\)-dimensional point in Cartesian space maps to a polygonal line intersecting \(m\) parallel axes, while a straight line in Cartesian space (\(y = mx + c\)) maps to a single pencil point of intersection between adjacent parallel coordinate axes.

docs.title: Q4. Why does Edward Tufte criticize the use of 3D bar charts?
docs.text: Answer: 3D bar charts introduce perspective foreshortening (foreground bars appear deceptively larger than identical background bars), occlude shorter bars in rear rows, create visual chartjunk, and reduce the Data-Ink ratio without adding informational value.

docs.title: Q5. What is the practical dimensional ceiling for Dimensional Stacking, and why?
docs.text: Answer: The practical ceiling is \(\le 9\) dimensions. Beyond nine dimensions, recursive embedding produces microscopic inner cells whose internal geometries cannot be resolved on standard screen resolutions, and human cognitive capacity cannot track the nested hierarchies.

docs.title: Q1. Compare Peano-Hilbert curves with Line-by-Line (Raster) scanning in pixel-oriented visualization.
docs.text:
Answer:

Evaluation Dimension Line-by-Line (Raster) Scanning Peano-Hilbert Space-Filling Curve Traversal Trajectory Horizontal left-to-right sweep across each row, followed by an abrupt return jump to the next row. Recursive fractal U-shaped orthogonal turns throughout \(2^k \times 2^k\) quadrants. Locality Preservation Poor. Records that are adjacent in 1D order across row boundaries are separated by the full width of the screen. Superior. Trajectory preserves multi-directional spatial proximity; neighbors in 1D remain neighbors in 2D. Visual Artifacts Introduces artificial horizontal banding and visual tearing at screen edges. Produces smooth, organic, contiguous spatial color patches representing clusters. Cluster Detection Fractures multi-dimensional clusters across row breaks, making small anomalies invisible. Consolidates multi-dimensional clusters into visible compact geometric patches. Computational Complexity Trivial (\(O(1)\) coordinate calculation: \(x = i \pmod W, y = \lfloor i/W \rfloor\)). Requires recursive bitwise quadtree decomposition (\(O(\log N)\) coordinate calculation).

docs.title: Q2. Explain the fundamental architectural failure of Seaborn when generating Stacked Bar Charts, and how Pandas and Altair solve this problem.
docs.text:
Answer:

  • Seaborn's Architectural Limitation: Seaborn is designed around statistical analysis of unaggregated tidy (long-format) data. In sns.barplot(), assigning a categorical attribute to hue automatically splits the visual marks into clustered (side-by-side) bars along the categorical axis. Seaborn possesses no native parameter (stacked=True does not exist in Seaborn) to stack these bars vertically on top of each other. Attempting to force a stacked bar chart in Seaborn requires tedious, manual calculation of multiple overlaid bar plots.
  • Pandas Solution: Pandas solves this by reshaping the DataFrame from tidy to wide format using .pivot(index='user_id', columns='website', values='number_chats'). Once reshaped, Pandas provides a native one-line plotting command: df.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True), which automatically stacks column segments along the vertical axis.
  • Altair Solution: Altair solves this elegantly through declarative visual encodings. The analyst specifies x='user_id:N', y='sum(number_chats):Q', and color='website:N'. Because Altair implements the Vega-Lite grammar of graphics, it automatically detects that multiple color marks occupy the same \(X\) coordinate and defaults to vertical stacking without requiring any data reshaping or pivoting.

docs.title: Part C: 10–15 Mark Enterprise System Design Problem
Problem Statement:
docs.text: An enterprise software corporation with 5,000 employees across 10 international subsidiaries is experiencing a sudden spike in voluntary engineering attrition and gender pay equity complaints. The Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO) commissions you as Lead Data Architect to design an Enterprise Human Capital Diagnostics & Compensation Parity Dashboard in Tableau.

docs.title: Comprehensive Solution Requirements:
docs.text:
Your design must provide:

  1. Architectural Pipeline & Data Model: Schema design, data sources, ingestion strategy, and Level of Detail (LOD) formulas.
  2. Dashboard Wireframe & Component Layout: Complete ASCII/Mermaid wireframe, hero BAN cards, and primary analytical sheets.
  3. KPI Taxonomy & Mathematical Formulations: Explicit formulas for the core metrics.
  4. Interactive Action Filters & Diagnostic Drill-Down Flow: How executive users interact with the dashboard to uncover root causes.

docs.title: 1. Architectural Pipeline & Data Model
docs.text:
• Data Sources: Core HRIS (Workday / SAP SuccessFactors) containing employee rosters; Enterprise Payroll (ADP) containing historical base, bonus, and equity compensation; and Applicant Tracking System (Greenhouse) containing recruitment funnel metrics.
  • Schema Design (Star Schema):
  • Fact Table: Fact_Employee_Monthly_Snapshot (Grain: 1 record per employee per calendar month). Attributes: Employee_SK, Date_Key, Base_Salary, Total_Comp, Bonus, Performance_Rating, Tenure_Months, Sick_Days, Voluntary_Exit_Flag.
  • Dimension Tables: Dim_Employee, Dim_Department, Dim_Job_Role, Dim_Location_Country, Dim_Demographics (Gender, Ethnicity, Age).
  • Tableau Calculated Fields & LOD Formulas:
  • Baseline Department Average Salary (Independent of Active Sheet Gender Filters): 
    [Dept_Avg_Salary_LOD] = { FIXED [Department], [Job_Level] : AVG([Base_Salary]) }
  • Gender Pay Gap Percentage: 
    [Gender_Pay_Gap_%] =
(AVG(IIF([Gender]="Female", [Base_Salary], NULL)) - AVG(IIF([Gender]="Male", [Base_Salary], NULL)))
/ AVG(IIF([Gender]="Male", [Base_Salary], NULL)) * 100.0
  • Annualized Voluntary Attrition Rate: 
    [Voluntary_Attrition_Rate] =
(SUM([Voluntary_Exit_Flag]) / { FIXED : COUNTD([Employee_ID]) }) * 12.0 * 100.0

docs.title: 3. Mathematical Formulas Used in Design
docs.text:
1. Gender Pay Gap Percentage:
\[ \text{Pay Gap} = \frac{\bar{W}_{\text{female}} - \bar{W}_{\text{male}}}{\bar{W}_{\text{male}}} \times 100\% \]

Where \(\bar{W}\) is average base compensation.

  1. Voluntary Attrition Rate:
\[ \text{Attrition Rate} = \frac{\sum \text{Voluntary Separations}}{\frac{1}{2}(\text{Headcount}_{\text{start}} + \text{Headcount}_{\text{end}})} \times 100\% \]
  1. Human Capital ROI (HCROI):
\[ \text{HCROI} = \frac{\text{Revenue} - (\text{Operating Expenses} - \text{Total Labor Costs})}{\text{Total Labor Costs}} \]

docs.title: 4. Interactive Action Filters & Diagnostic Drill-Down Flow
docs.text:
1. Executive Overview (Level 1): The CHRO opens the dashboard and immediately views the hero BAN cards. The red flag on Gender Pay Gap (-3.9%) and Voluntary Exits (8.4%) confirms institutional risk.
  2. Visual Cross-Filtering (Level 2): Clicking the Senior Manager bar on Sheet 1 activates a Tableau Filter Action that updates Sheet 2 and Sheet 3. Sheet 2 dynamically isolates Senior Management roles, revealing that the female senior manager pay deficit expands to -8.2% in Engineering.
  3. Cohort Root-Cause Isolation (Level 3): Clicking the deep-red 15.4% attrition cell on Sheet 2 (Tenure: 3–5 Years, Performance Band C) triggers another filter action on Sheet 3.
  4. Operational Remediation (Level 4): Sheet 3 displays the exact roster of affected engineers, their specific managers, salary differentials relative to the {FIXED Department, Job_Level : AVG(Salary)} LOD benchmark, and flight-risk scores. The CHRO exports this filtered list directly to the compensation committee for targeted salary adjustment, resolving pay inequity before talent attrition occurs.

[Source: Synthesis of Unit3_Data Visualization.pdf, Slides 34–46; DAV_Tableau.md, Sections 4–7]

docs.text:

docs.title: 1. Section Narrative Spines: Conceptual Flow and Logical Architecture
docs.text:
Modern data analysis pipelines are confronted with massive data collections characterized by millions of records (massive row volumes) and hundreds or thousands of attributes (high dimensionality). When submitted directly to analytical algorithms or visualization engines, such raw datasets introduce severe computational bottlenecks, algorithm convergence failures, storage strain, and cognitive overload for human analysts.

Unit 4 establishes the formal engineering paradigm of Data Reduction and Feature Enhancement. The logical progression of this unit is structured into three interconnected conceptual pillars:

  1. Foundations of Data Reduction: Establishing why data volume must be reduced while preserving underlying information content, exploring the 4 fundamental engineering goals, and organizing all known reduction methods into a structured master taxonomy.
  2. Statistical Sampling Principles: Developing the theoretical and mathematical framework for selecting representative row subsets (numerosity reduction) from massive populations, differentiating probability from non-probability paradigms, analyzing critical caveats such as database physical page I/O constraints and distribution skewness, and tracing the 5-step sampling lifecycle.
  3. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) & Feature Enhancement: Addressing the column dimension (dimensionality reduction) through linear algebra and eigendecomposition, discovering optimal orthogonal axes that maximize preserved variance, executing a complete 10–15 mark numerical exam calculation, and mapping the theory to Python and KNIME software toolchains.
flowchart TD
